prize_parts.citation: For chemically induced proximity that directs proteins to the ubiquitin-proteasome system for degradation, through heterobifunctional PROTACs and the identification of cereblon as the target of molecular-glue degraders

statement.case_for: Targeted degradation turns a biological process, ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis, into a designable chemical reaction. A small molecule brings a target and an E3 ligase together, and the result is removal of the protein, not inhibition. The principle is general and mechanistically well defined, supported by ternary-complex structures and kinetics, and it has been reproduced by many independent laboratories on many targets. It gives biologists a tool to deplete proteins acutely, and it gives medicine a new modality. Three members ranked it first and it is the broadest-supported entry on the shortlist. I also find the cereblon mechanism persuasive because it explained, after decades, how thalidomide acts, and that is the kind of molecular explanation I want to see behind a prize.
statement.case_against: The credit is crowded. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim, Ito and others made decisive contributions, and a three-person cut will leave out people whom many would regard as founders of a sub-arm. The PROTAC and molecular-glue streams have different histories and may not belong in a single sentence. Clinical validation is still incomplete, and whether degraders deliver durable efficacy and safety in patients is not settled. The first Crews and Deshaies PROTAC used a peptide ligand with poor cell permeability, so the early demonstrations were proof of concept and the practical drug-like version came later.

responses.point: Aqvist anchors the prize on PROTACs with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, and says the glue arm (Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Gray, Kim) is a competing credit stream that cannot fit in three.
responses.response: I agree the glue arm is a separate credit stream, but I would still put Handa in the third seat instead of Ciulli. Without the cereblon identification the glue arm has no mechanism, and it links the concept to a drug that has been in the clinic for decades. Ciulli's VHL ligands and structural work are important and make PROTACs drug-like, and I accept that this is the most contestable choice on my ballot. The two proposals differ only on the third name, which I take as a sign that the underlying case for B019 is stable.

responses.point: Linke ranks nanopore sequencing first for its clear physical principle and its long-read, label-free capability, and ranks degraders fourth.
responses.response: The physical principle in nanopores is clean, and the technology is mature, which I respect. My reservation is attribution. Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Akeson and Bayley contributed different pieces (translocation, ratcheting, engineered pores), and I cannot see a defensible three-person cut that I would trust. Degraders have a comparable problem, but the Crews, Deshaies and Handa trio maps better onto the two mechanistic pillars. I would also be interested to hear whether you think the nanopore sensing principle is chemistry rather than biophysics instrumentation.

responses.point: Aili ranks B019 first because bifunctional recognition and induced assembly is a general design principle, and ranks base editing second as a Liu-centred chemical biology invention.
responses.response: I share your first choice and your reading of the design principle. On base editing I am more reserved than you. David Liu's work is clearly chemical protein engineering, but the 2020 CRISPR prize makes it look like an extension of a field already recognised, and the Kondo and Nishida priority question remains open. It is my first fallback, but I would prefer it later.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks long-range electron transfer through proteins first as a physical mechanism of biological redox chains, and places degraders seventh.
responses.response: The Gray and Winkler tunnelling work is quantitative and well replicated, and the attribution is clean, which I value. My doubt is breadth. It refines how a known class of process works, whereas degraders created a new reaction and a new tool used well outside the field. I also note it follows the Marcus prize closely. I do not see it as weaker science, but I see a smaller scope of consequence.

uncertainties: Whether the prize should credit PROTACs and molecular glues as one achievement or split them, and if combined, whether the trio Crews, Deshaies, Handa is better than one including Ciulli or Gray
Whether clinical degrader outcomes will confirm durable benefit by the time of recognition
Whether Handa's cereblon identification is sufficiently independent of the earlier thalidomide work and of the Ito and Sakamoto contributions in the committee's eyes
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My work on nucleotide metabolism and genome stability at Umeå does not involve any candidate named on the shortlist, and I have no stated collaboration or institutional tie to them.
